source: BVTech edge telemetry + global threat patterns (representative 24h window; the Pulse portal refreshes this snapshot with live numbers)

types.name: Credential brute-force
types.what: Bots hammer login pages with millions of stolen or guessed username/password pairs, hunting for one reused credential.
types.defense: We enforce MFA, auto-lock accounts after repeated failures, and block the source IP at the edge after 3 strikes.

types.name: Automated vuln scanning
types.what: Scanners fingerprint your site for known holes — probing /wp-login.php, /.env, /.git/config — to find an easy way in.
types.defense: Our bot filter recognizes scanner signatures, honeypots swallow them, and we keep every system patched so the holes aren’t there.

types.name: Malware & exploit probes
types.what: Direct attempts to drop a web-shell or trigger remote code execution (phpunit RCE, shell uploads, router exploits).
types.defense: WAF rules reject the payloads, least-privilege blocks execution, and endpoint protection flags anything that lands.

types.name: Honeypot trips
types.what: Hits on decoy admin pages and logins that no real visitor ever touches — so anything that touches them is hostile by definition.
types.defense: A honeypot trip is an instant, automatic 24-hour edge ban — the attacker is gone before they reach anything real.
